pass_rule: all core questions substantially correct in the learner's own words; stretch questions inform the grade, not the gate

questions.prompt: os.File, net.Conn, bytes.Buffer, and gzip.Reader are wildly different things. Why can one io.Copy call work with all of them, and what does that buy you when you write your own functions?
expected_points: they all satisfy the tiny io.Reader/io.Writer interfaces
code written against the interface works with every source/destination, present and future
small interfaces are the composition points — accept io.Reader/io.Writer in your own APIs

questions.prompt: A Read call returns n = 5 and err = io.EOF at the same time. Is that reader broken? What must a correct caller do with that result?
expected_points: not broken — the contract explicitly allows n > 0 together with io.EOF
consume p[:n] first, then handle the error
checking err before consuming the data silently drops the final bytes of the stream
partial reads (n less than len(p)) are also normal, not errors

questions.prompt: Walk me through your UpperReader.Read: what do you delegate, what do you transform, and what do you pass through untouched? Why does the order of those steps matter?
expected_points: delegate the actual read to the wrapped reader
transform only p[:n] — the bytes actually delivered
transform before inspecting err so data arriving with io.EOF is kept
return the inner n and err unchanged — the adapter must not reinterpret the stream

questions.prompt: Pick the right tool and justify it: (a) assemble a string from many small pieces, (b) capture what some code writes for a test assertion, (c) write many small records to a file efficiently.
expected_points: (a) strings.Builder — write-only accumulator, copy-free String(), avoids quadratic concatenation
(b) bytes.Buffer — an in-memory io.Writer (and Reader) you can inspect
(c) bufio.Writer around the file — batches small writes into few syscalls, must Flush()

questions.prompt: Your Shout must handle a 10GB input on a small machine. Why does chaining NewUpperReader with io.Copy survive that when io.ReadAll would not?
expected_points: io.Copy pumps fixed-size chunks (a 32KB buffer) through the chain
memory use is constant regardless of stream size
io.ReadAll holds the entire payload in memory — proportional to input size
each stage of a chain touches chunks in flight; nobody holds the whole payload

questions.prompt: In CountingWriter.Write, why do you add the returned n to the count instead of len(p)?
expected_points: writers may perform short writes — accept fewer than len(p) bytes and return an error
n is what was actually written; len(p) is only what was requested
counting len(p) would overreport on any failing or partial write

questions.prompt: Your LineCount meets a log file containing a single 500KB line. What happens with your current code, and how would you fix it?
expected_points: bufio.Scanner's default max token size is 64KB — it stops with bufio.ErrTooLong
sc.Err() surfaces the error, so LineCount reports it rather than silently undercounting
raise the limit with Scanner.Buffer (or switch to bufio.Reader for unbounded lines)
